item.text:
# Félix Tshisekedi in 2024: 1B.4 research note

## Bottom line
The 2024 record supports a **qualified yes** on de-escalatory agreement support, but only in the **eastern DRC peace-process sense**. I found:

- **Positive evidence:** Tshisekedi publicly backed the Luanda process, a ceasefire with Rwanda, and broader regional peace talks.
- **Negative / limiting evidence:** the ceasefire repeatedly frayed, fighting resumed, and planned leader-level talks collapsed by December.
- **No meaningful evidence found** on arms-control, inspection, nonproliferation, or disarmament in the strict nuclear sense. For DRC in 2024, this lens is mostly about **ceasefire and regional de-escalation agreements**.

## Accepted claims

- [**Crise sécuritaire dans l’Est de la Rdc : Les Présidents Félix Tshisekedi Et Joao Lourenco appellent au respect du cessez-le-feu**](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/crise_securitaire_dans_lest_de_la_rdc_les_presidents_felix_tshisekedi_et_joao_lourenco_appellent_au_respect_du_cessez_le_feu)  
  - **Publisher:** Présidence RDC  
  - **Date:** 2024-08-12  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Tshisekedi met with Angola’s president, who was mediating the Luanda process, and both sides welcomed the 4 August ceasefire and said it should be respected. This is direct evidence that Tshisekedi publicly supported a de-escalation agreement.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.4, 1B.1

- [**Readout of the Secretary-General’s meeting with H.E. Mr. Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo**](https://www.un.org/sg/en/content/sg/readouts/2024-09-24/readout-of-the-secretary-generals-meeting-he-mr-felix-antoine-tshisekedi-tshilombo-president-of-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-scroll-down-for-french)  
  - **Publisher:** UN Secretary-General  
  - **Date:** 2024-09-24  
  - **Claim-level summary:** The UN said Tshisekedi discussed eastern DRC and ongoing regional peace efforts with the Secretary-General, who reiterated support for regional peace initiatives. This is independent confirmation that Tshisekedi was participating in peace-process diplomacy rather than rejecting it.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.4, 1B.1

- [**Security Council Briefing on MONUSCO by Special Representative of the Secretary-General Bintou Keita**](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en/node/132163)  
  - **Publisher:** UN Peacekeeping  
  - **Date:** 2024-09-30  
  - **Claim-level summary:** The UN reported that after the 30 July ceasefire announcement, fighting between the parties sharply decreased and an active framework for dialogue was underway, supported by Angolan mediation. This does not prove Tshisekedi alone drove the outcome, but it supports the claim that his government was engaged in a genuine de-escalatory framework.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.4, 1B.1

- [**Processus de Luanda : La tripartite n’aura plus lieu**](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/processus_de_luanda_la_tripartite_naura_plus_lieu)  
  - **Publisher:** Présidence RDC  
  - **Date:** 2024-12-15  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Tshisekedi went to Luanda for the planned tripartite, but the meeting collapsed after Rwanda declined to participate and demanded direct DRC-M23 dialogue. This is relevant counterevidence: Tshisekedi supported talks, but the process failed to produce an agreement, which weakens any strong good-faith success reading.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.4, 1B.1

- [**Fighting resumes in eastern Congo, army and M23 say**](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Fighting-resumes-in-eastern-Congo-army-and-M23-say-48510597/)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** 2024-12-03  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported that fighting resumed in eastern Congo in violation of a ceasefire, casting doubt on whether the M23 offensive would stop after earlier disengagement steps. This is not direct proof of Tshisekedi bad faith, but it is strong evidence that the de-escalation framework was not holding in practice by late 2024.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.4, 1B.1

## Search gap

- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Tshisekedi engaged in formal **arms-control, inspection, nonproliferation, or disarmament** policy in the nuclear sense.
- The only substantive material was about **regional ceasefires, Luanda/Nairobi-style peace processes, and conflict de-escalation in eastern Congo**.
- So the defensible conclusion is **qualified support for de-escalation agreements**, but **limited proof of durable good-faith implementation** because the process repeatedly stalled and fighting resumed.
